correctness.rationale: On the exact parameter slice, direct differentiation gives \(\dot H=-gx^2\) with no omitted terms. For bounded forward solutions, monotone convergence of \(H\), square-integrability and uniform continuity of \(x\), and invariance of the omega-limit set force convergence to a single equilibrium. For compact invariant measures, \(\int LH\,d\mu=0\) forces support on \(x=0\), and invariance successively forces \(y=v=u=0\). Exact rational replay verifies the source-parameter coefficient and Jacobian characteristic polynomial. The proof does not infer infinite-time behavior from a finite experiment.

value.rationale: The result resolves a mathematically consequential ambiguity in a published line-equilibrium chaos example: a simple exact Lyapunov identity excludes every non-equilibrium compact recurrent state on the whole slice, not merely at one initial condition. It also classifies all compact invariant probability measures and explains why positive finite-time tangent growth can coexist with a constant equilibrium trajectory. Because line-equilibrium chaos is possible in other systems, this is a substantive system-specific structural obstruction rather than a generic textbook deduction from the existence of an equilibrium line.
